props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who says 'on a bird's nest may Your mercy reach' -- they silence him
the mishna: one who says 'on the good may Your name be mentioned' -- they silence him
the mishna: one who says 'we give thanks, we give thanks' -- they silence him
'we give thanks, we give thanks' -- because it looks like two authorities
'on the good may Your name be mentioned' too -- it implies: on the good yes, on the bad no
and we learned: a person must bless on the bad just as he blesses on the good
because he casts jealousy among the works of creation
because he makes the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He, mercy, and they are nothing but decrees
the leader before Rabba: 'You had pity on the bird's nest -- have pity and mercy on us!' (the bracketed text adds: 'You had pity on it and its young')
Rabba: how well this scholar knows how to appease his Master!
and Rabba -- he wanted to sharpen Abaye
the leader before R' Chanina: 'the great, mighty and awesome God, the powerful, the strong and the fearless'
R' Chanina: have you finished your Master's praises? ... and you say all this!
even these three -- had Moses not written them in the Torah and the Great Assembly come and fixed them, we would not say them
a parable: a man who had thousands upon thousands of gold dinars, and they praised him for (a thousand) silver dinars -- is it not a disgrace to him?
R' Chanina: everything is in the hands of Heaven except fear of Heaven
as it says: 'and now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear' (Deut 10:12)
Moses: 'what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear' -- read by the stam (מכלל, 25a.10) as presenting fear of Heaven as a small matter
yes -- for Moses our teacher it is a small matter
a parable: one asked for a large vessel which he has -- it seems to him like a small vessel; a small one which he has not -- it seems to him like a large vessel
R' Zeira: one who says 'shema, shema' is like one who says 'modim, modim'
the baraita: one who reads the Shema and doubles it -- this is reprehensible
the baraita (reprehensible only) is one who says [each] word and repeats it
R' Zeira (silenced) is one who says [each] verse and repeats it
Rava: familiarity toward Heaven?! if he did not direct his mind, we strike him with a smith's hammer until he directs his mind
